description:
Discover candidate products for a buyer need. Takes a need in natural language (e.g. "best value home espresso machine", market "TH"), Unless the need is out of scope or live discovery is off or rate-limited, each call reads the verified catalog and also runs live web discovery, which sends the need text to web-search providers. A confirmed live result is returned when there is one; catalog candidates are returned instead when live discovery is unavailable, rate-limited, fails, or confirms no fit. Returns up to 3 candidates with explicit fit accounting.

find_products is the quick candidate-list tool; research_shopping is the full verified-research job. For a specific brand+model, search_catalog is cheaper and returns the same live-lookup block on a miss.

Response fields:
• candidates[].verification — "catalog-verified" for a catalog row whose stated requirements each have a receipt, "catalog-candidate" for a catalog starting point whose fit still needs checking, or "live-unverified" for a live page read during this run.
• candidates[].status — "resolved" means both identity and the parsed buyer constraints were supported by the cited page; "abstain" means identity or need fit could not be established. Inspect constraint_check for matched, conflicting, and unverified requirements.
• candidates[].constraint_check.receipts maps each receipt-backed matched requirement to its supporting source URL and trust label.
• Live candidates come from current web-search results, so they are a sample of what the market offers rather than a ranking.
• status at the top level — "no_match" means no candidate was confirmed as satisfying the need; "disabled" means live discovery is off and no candidates are returned; "rate_limited" or "unavailable" means no discovery ran and no catalog candidate was found.

• live_discovery.status="unavailable" means receipted catalog candidates were returned while live discovery was unavailable.

Optional `market` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country and scopes the lookup cache. "Available in <market>" means the seller page serves that market, not that stock is guaranteed.

market.description: Buyer market as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. "TH"). Biases discovery and marketplace checks toward seller pages serving that country and scopes the cache; availability is not a stock guarantee.

max.description: Max candidates to verify (each costs a live lookup; capped at 3).

need.description: The buyer need in natural language, e.g. "quiet mechanical keyboard for open office" or "best value home espresso machine".

name: find_products
title: Discover and verify products for a need
